control_ab_summary: Certified Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B AXQ-6bit/4bit-MTP packs (Tier 2 certified on engine 6.14.1, formal suites) re-run on the same 7.5.4 binary, same dev suites, same profile: AXQ6 agent-coding passes exact (1.3279x) but general-long is inexact (1.0447x/1.0883x); AXQ4 fails exactness on both profiles (1.3336x/0.9436x). The 7.5.4 verify path is therefore not row-exact against direct decode engine-wide, independent of pack format: an engine regression from the 6.14.1 generation is the primary root-cause candidate, with pack/format modulation on top.
determinism_probe_summary: Same prompt repeated 8x per arm, all four packs: every direct arm and every MTP arm is internally bit-deterministic (256/256 generations), so decode itself is not jittery. Cross-arm first-divergence is identical across all 8 pairs per prompt (e.g. cyber-tiel agent-coding prompt 1 always at token 21) but varies prompt to prompt and pack to pack (9 exact / 7 verify-differs / 0 nondeterministic). The verify path computes deterministically different logits than the direct path on specific prompts; this is a row-exactness defect, not run-to-run noise.
engine_dev_build_finding: The in-tree AX Engine dev build on df-macbookpro-m5 (v7.5.4-40-g875da6b5, Aug 19 2026) never activates MTP for these packs (ax_mtp_requested=1, ax_mtp_available=0, qwen_linear_mtp_exact_eligible=0, mtp_model_gate_default_present=0 on every trial). The 7.5.4 release binary enables MTP on the same host/packs. Recorded as an engine-side regression candidate for the >=7.5.5 development line; not an AXQuant pack property.

engine_version_bisect.certification_conclusion: Tiel: not certifiable on any available engine build (inexact wherever its MTP head loads). Cyber-Tiel: the agent-coding profile passes all Tier 2 gates on the factory host under 7.5.4 (exact 2/2, 1.2088x/1.2088x), but a certified Tier 2 requires a certified Tier 1 (publication governance in public_cert_index), and Cyber-Tiel's Tier 1 is not_certified on the checkpoint quality gate (retention 0.9615 < 0.98 vs the pinned quantized source). The scoped pass is therefore recorded here as measured evidence but is NOT issued as a certificate. Paths: raise checkpoint quality above the Tier 1 gate (source/convert decision), or accept no Tier 2 for this edition.
engine_version_bisect.layout_finding: The packs' mtplx_runtime.json declares mtp_norm_layout raw_hf_delta, but all MTP norms are already converted (original+1) — the September 19 Tiel exports failure mode documented in docs/guides/preserved-mtp-norm-layout.md. AX Engine's compatibility correction binds to the complete hashes of those two audited sidecars; it exists only on the 7.5.x line (present v7.5.0/v7.5.4, absent v7.4.0 and earlier, broken again by v7.5.4+40). Engines without the shim never load the MTP head (policy None, ax_mtp_available=0), so the packs' exactness is only testable on 7.5.x — where this pack is inexact on both profiles even though the certified AXQ control pack stays exact on agent-coding. A metadata-corrected revision (mlx_multiplier, byte-identical weights) would load natively but still faces the engine-wide general-long row-exactness regression on every engine that supports MXFP4.

v6.14.1.note: predates MXFP4 exact-MTP verify support (landed after v6.14.0)

v7.5.4+40 (dev).note: gate regression candidate on the >=7.5.5 line

engine_version_bisect.method: Built ax-engine-bench from source worktrees at release tags on df-macbookpro-m5 (v7.1.1/v7.3.0 against mlx 0.32.0, v7.3.0+ against mlx 0.32.2 per each tree's mlx.version pin) and ran the same Tier 2 A/B harness, dev suites, seed, and exact profile. Activation = ax_mtp_available on MTP-on trials; exactness = greedy MTP-vs-direct token match on the measured prompts.

revised_root_cause: Primary: AX Engine 7.5.4 verify-path row-exactness regression vs 6.14.1 (control packs fail too). Secondary: pack/format modulation (MXFP4 MoE packs fail more profiles than AXQ controls in the same runs). Host ruled out as the cause (same binary, both hosts, deterministic per host).
summary: Same AX Engine 7.5.4 release binary (sha256 eeb40413...) and same packs, datasets, seed, and runtime profile on both hosts. MTP engages on both (ax_mtp_available=1). Greedy exactness between MTP and direct decode fails on both hosts on both packs except cyber-tiel agent-coding on the factory host; divergent trials and first-divergence positions differ by host, which is the signature of numeric (not logical) divergence in the multi-token verify path on these MXFP4 MoE packs. M5 Max decode is ~1.5x faster than M2 Ultra; agent-coding speedups clear 1.20x on M5 Max but general-long stays under the 1.20x floor on both hosts.
